entities.name: Nafi ibn al-Azraq
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nafi ibn al-Azraq ibn Qays al-Hanafi al-Bakri was a pivotal leader of the Kharijite faction of the Azariqa during the tumultuous Second Fitna of 680-683 CE. A native of the Arabian Peninsula, Nafi's significance extends to the broader Middle Eastern context, where his actions played a crucial role in the schism of the Islamic community.


The core events surrounding Nafi's leadership revolved around his participation in the Second Fitna, a period marked by intense sectarian violence and power struggles. Nafi's faction, the Azariqa, clashed with the opposing faction led by Mus'ab ibn Zam'a, resulting in the eventual defeat of the Azariqa and Nafi's exile.


The legacy of Nafi ibn al-Azraq can be seen in the long-term consequences of the Second Fitna, which set the stage for the eventual rise of the Abbasid Caliphate. As a result, Nafi's actions had a lasting impact on the Islamic world, influencing the trajectory of the community's internal dynamics and shaping the course of subsequent historical events.


A testament to Nafi's enduring influence lies in the numerous accounts of his exploits, as recorded by prominent historians such as Ibn al-Athir and Ibn Khaldun. These sources not only provide valuable insight into Nafi's life and actions but also underscore the significance of his role in shaping the Islamic world.
